replacement.limits: Static experimental practice scene. Positions are examples and do not prove timing, execution, possession outcome, or a universal team system; coaching responses are ungraded.

questions.prompt: After the entry pass, which Navy player is the carrier?
questions.explanation: The setup assigns possession to F2 after the entry pass.

questions.prompt: Which two details matter when filling high support?

options.text: A high support spot chosen without checking F2’s lane

questions.explanation: Support follows the carrier and coverage; a fixed spot can crowd or disconnect the play.

questions.prompt: Arrange the post-entry support change.

options.text: Find F2 and the inside coverage

questions.explanation: Finding F2 and the inside coverage can overlap with skating to the new lane; a player keeps scanning while moving. The final re-check still comes last because it depends on where the play has actually gone once the lane is offered.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot support example after F2 receives.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU from (20,8) to (15,4), about 6.4 m. With x=15 behind F2 at x=19 toward Navy’s end, it illustrates a higher support relationship while remaining separate from the carrier; it does not prove a reachable or visible connection, so recheck F2 and the defenders.

questions.prompt: F2 loses the puck to A2. What takes priority?

options.text: Re-read the transition and recover toward the dangerous lane
Assume the entry is still controlled

questions.explanation: Possession changed, so the role changes before the old support route is continued.

questions.prompt: Which support space did YOU fill, and what route does it leave F2?
questions.explanation: Describe the high-slot relationship and a possible return route for F2. The example does not prove that an outlet is visible or reachable; if Gold closes the lane, re-offer from another checked angle.

changedQuestions.reason: Q1 text itself has no defect (F2 is correctly the carrier per setup.puck.owner=h2, and F3/YOU are plausible non-giveaway distractors). Marked repair, not retain, because the scene-level briefing/cue grammar and roster-naming fix (see repair record) changes this question’s content hash under the mandatory scene+question hash function; the original baseContentHash no longer describes final content. Measured/visible: h1 labeled YOU, team home, at (20,8), facing -1.7 h2 labeled F2, team home, at (19,0), facing 0, owns the puck Stated: Briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net; after F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone; D1 is nearer the blue line

Q2 text itself has no defect. Options a/b name real, load-bearing factors (F2’s puck position, Gold’s inside coverage); option c follows the bank’s established "narrow focus" distractor pattern (compare example-batch.json q2) and is not a giveaway. Marked repair only for the same cascading scene-hash reason as q1. Measured/visible: h1 labeled YOU, team home, at (20,8), facing -1.7 h2 labeled F2, team home, at (19,0), facing 0, owns the puck Stated: Briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net; after F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone; D1 is nearer the blue line

Genuine defect: the sequence (find F2/coverage -> offer separated high lane -> re-check carrier/exit) is fine to keep as an answer key, but its explanation implied a strict look-then-move-then-recheck order. AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md explicitly warns against implying an artificial look/decide/execute order for reads that can overlap. Repaired the explanation (kept the same order/answer) to disclose that scanning for F2/coverage and skating into the new lane can happen at the same time, while explaining why the final re-check still has to come last. Measured/visible: h1 labeled YOU, team home, at (20,8), facing -1.7 h2 labeled F2, team home, at (19,0), facing 0, owns the puck Stated: Briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net; after F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone; D1 is nearer the blue line
Moved the high-support example to (15,4), measured relative to F2 at (19,0), and removed claims that the connection or defenders are necessarily visible.

Genuine defect: the prompt named "Gold 2" as the player who takes the puck from F2, but no actor in setup.actors carries that label (away skaters are D1, A1, A2). This is the wrong-named-actor / internal roster contradiction pattern called out in lesson 12 and the historical "wrong named actor or absent teammate" check. A player reading the rendered scene would see "A2", never "Gold 2". Repaired the prompt to name "A2", matching the briefing fix. Measured/visible: h1 labeled YOU, team home, at (20,8), facing -1.7 h2 labeled F2, team home, at (19,0), facing 0, owns the puck Stated: Briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net; after F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone; D1 is nearer the blue line
Made the outlet explicitly possible and conditional on a checked lane.
